Metadata.xiaozuDescription: Xiaozu: an AI coach and playing partner for chess lovers. Sync moves by hand on any platform, mirror your screen for whole-board recognition every second, or share a link to play a friend live — lighting up the strongest move before you commit.

hero.title: Chinese Chess AI Assistant
hero.tagline: A small pawn can change the game
hero.description: A personal AI coach and playing partner for every Chinese chess lover. Before you commit a move, Xiaozu reads the position and lights up the strongest option — play with more confidence, review with more clarity, and sharpen your game one match at a time.

usage.title: Three ways, your choice
usage.lead: Whatever platform you play on, Xiaozu keeps up: enter moves by hand with zero setup, or mirror your screen and let it read the whole board every second and tell you exactly what to play — or spin up a link and play a friend live from anywhere.

methods.title: Manual sync
methods.summary: Play your moves and enter your opponent's on Xiaozu's web board — the engine recommends in real time.
bullets: Works on any platform, from WeChat mini-programs to JJ Xiangqi
No extra tools to install — zero dependencies
You move, you log the opponent's move, the position syncs instantly
The engine analyzes and recommends your best move live

methods.title: Screen-mirror recognition
methods.summary: Mirror your phone to your computer; a local sidecar reads the whole board every second, syncs to the web, and gives you your move.
bullets: Play normally on your phone — the board is recognized about once a second
Auto-synced to the web, no manual entry
Any position or endgame works — no need to start from move one
Always guides your side; red/black switches automatically

methods.title: Live remote match
methods.summary: Send a link or QR code to a friend — one tap and they're seated for a live remote match; the host can hand any move to the AI at any time.
bullets: Share a link or QR code — no install, your opponent taps in and sits down
Both sides sync in real time; every move shows instantly, like playing in person
The host can switch on AI stand-in anytime and let the engine respond
Perfect for far-away friends and long-distance matches — start anytime

items.title: AI coach

items.desc: In mirror mode it reads your side and tells you exactly what to play.

Apps.installTitle: How to add to your home screen
Apps.installLead: These are PWAs (Progressive Web Apps) — no app store needed; just open the page and add it as a home-screen icon.
Apps.iosSteps: Open the app in Safari → tap the Share button → choose "Add to Home Screen" → done. The icon appears on your home screen and opens like a native app.
Apps.androidSteps: Open the app in Chrome → tap the top-right menu → choose "Install app / Add to Home screen" → done. An "Install" prompt may also appear in the address bar.

Dpp.metaTitle: EU Digital Product Passport implementation — Murphy Cloud
Dpp.metaDescription: DPP implementation for Chinese manufacturers: readiness assessment, product data architecture, open-dpp based platform delivery, and pilot validation.

hero.badge: EU Digital Product Passport · implementation partner
hero.title: Give every product a trusted <accent>digital identity</accent>
hero.description: We help Chinese manufacturers meet the EU Digital Product Passport at a workable cost — from regulatory assessment and data architecture through to platform rollout.

industries.label: Built for the sectors DPP regulation reaches first

why.title: The compliance window is narrowing — now is the moment to build the data capability
why.lead: DPP is not a QR-code project. It is a system upgrade spanning products, supply chain, and data governance.

items.title: The EU requires it
items.desc: ESPR is now in force. Batteries, textiles, and electronics will be phased into mandatory digital product passports.

items.title: Supply-chain transparency is the entry ticket
items.desc: Traceable data from raw material to recycling is becoming a baseline requirement for selling into Europe.

items.title: Circularity creates new value
items.desc: Trustworthy product data supports repair, reuse, recycling, and new service models — value that keeps compounding.

items.title: Build once, reuse everywhere
items.desc: A single data foundation can serve DPP, PCF, CSRD, and CBAM disclosure requirements at the same time.

authority.title: Knowing the regulation is not enough — we know how to <accent>make it run</accent>
authority.description: Real DPP capability sits where regulation, engineering practice, and open-source influence meet. Fifteen years of enterprise architecture and supply-chain work, distilled into a method you can verify.
authority.quote: We are not observers studying DPP. We are upstream practitioners on open-dpp.

items.title: From regulation to running system
items.desc: We translate ESPR, the Battery Regulation, and their peers into concrete data fields, processes, and system architecture.

items.title: Upstream on open-dpp
items.desc: We don't just explain DPP — we deliver working engineering built on public upstream contributions, code, and API evolution.

items.title: Supply-chain data governance
items.desc: Enterprise architecture, cross-border supply chain, and data governance experience, so the passport connects to the systems you already run.

items.title: AI-assisted passport build-out
items.desc: Regulatory Q&A, spec-sheet and document parsing, automatic field generation and completion, compliance checks — the repetitive data work handled by AI.

WorkGraph.metaTitle: WorkGraph - Task Graph Collaboration (the WorkSync upgrade)
WorkGraph.metaDescription: WorkGraph is the WorkSync upgrade: a semantic task platform where tasks are nodes, relationships are edges, and templates are the ontology. The task graph shows who is blocking whom; docs, diagrams, whiteboards, attachments and external links share one mechanism; webhooks and a JSON-LD read API project the graph to other systems.

hero.badge: The WorkSync upgrade · the full loop is live
hero.title: Tasks are not a list. <accent>They are a graph you can query.</accent>
hero.description: WorkGraph treats tasks as nodes, relationships as edges and templates as the ontology. Beyond parent/child hierarchy there are dependency, blocking and reference edges - so "who is blocking whom" is no longer something people have to remember. It can be queried, drawn, and subscribed to by other systems.
hero.shotCaption: Task graph · horizontal axis is dependency order, dashed frames are hierarchy

floatTwo.title: Red dashed edge
floatTwo.desc: A dependency cycle - drawn, not thrown as an error

diff.title: Three differences from list-style tools
diff.lead: These are not three lines on a feature list. They are three modelling decisions, and they decide which questions the product can answer.

items.title: A task has an ontology, not just a title
items.desc: Each kind of task (bug, requirement, review...) gets a template that defines its fields, and a task is an instance of that template. Editing a template never rewrites existing tasks - every instance remembers the version it was created from.
items.note: The task detail page says bug · v3

items.title: Tasks form a graph, not a list
items.desc: On top of hierarchy, tasks carry dependency, blocking and reference edges. "Who is blocking whom" becomes something you query and draw, instead of something someone recites in a standup.

items.title: A project is a hard boundary
items.desc: A project you are not a member of does not exist for you: the answer is 404, not 403. Global admins are no exception - task visibility always goes through project membership, so an admin has to join first, and joining is audited.

diff.figureCaption: Concept map · every box is a real object in the product

line.title: One main line, seven steps to a full loop
line.lead: From getting in to projecting out, the product has exactly one main line. Everything else hangs off the side of it.

steps.title: Access
steps.desc: Sign in with email and password. The project switcher in the top bar decides whose data a page lists; the sidebar is filtered by permission - entries you cannot see are not disabled, your role simply does not have them.

steps.title: Pick the ontology
steps.desc: Choose a template before filling in a form. The template decides what the form looks like, and how this kind of task can be counted later.

steps.title: Create the task
steps.desc: The form is generated from the template, with custom fields to cover whatever the template does not.

steps.title: Wire up the graph
steps.desc: Attach parents (up to 8 levels, never to itself or its own descendants) and draw dependency, blocking and reference edges. This step is where the product diverges from a to-do list.

steps.title: Move it forward
steps.desc: Four states: not started, in progress, done, blocked. The board is drag-and-drop, and progress rolls up as a plain average of direct children - deliberately unweighted, so when you need an exact figure you read the numbers, not the percentage.

steps.title: Finish
steps.desc: Tasks with unfinished predecessors show a lock badge. There is no realtime co-editing, but saving does a version check, so nobody's edit is silently overwritten.

steps.title: Semantic projection
steps.desc: Project the graph outward: webhook events and a JSON-LD read API let other systems subscribe to task changes.

shots.caption: Templates as ontology · field definitions first, instances second
Hierarchy · up to 8 levels, progress averaged over direct children

graph.title: See <accent>who is blocking whom</accent> on one screen
graph.lead: Hand-drawn SVG with ELK layout - not an exported static picture. Horizontal is dependency order, dashed frames are hierarchy; node fill is status, the left bar is priority, the icon is type.

legend.v: Aggregated edge across a collapsed subtree
Hover highlight of the whole transitive chain

caps.title: Filtering never deletes nodes
caps.desc: Non-matching nodes fade instead of disappearing, and the corner shows "X of Y matched". You always know which part of the whole you are looking at.

caps.title: A screen you can send as-is
caps.desc: Focus mode keeps ancestors, descendants and transitive dependencies; filter, focus and collapse state all live in the URL query, so a colleague opens exactly the screen you were looking at.

caps.title: Four export outlets
caps.desc: Download SVG, download PNG at 2x, copy the PlantUML source, or save it as a project diagram. The first three happen entirely in the browser - the graph never leaves it.

caps.title: Keyboard and screen readers work
caps.desc: Tab and Enter navigate; clicking a node opens a peek drawer. A plain-text list of nodes and dependencies ships alongside, so a screen reader never has to chew through the SVG.

graph.shotCaption: Click a node for a peek drawer · the thumbnail lists predecessors | this task | successors, up to four each

resources.title: Docs, diagrams, whiteboards, attachments and links are five kinds of one object
resources.lead: The five modules you know from WorkSync are five kinds of a single resource mechanism here: one permission model, one trash, one way to share. Not five subsystems each solving it again.

items.title: Document library
items.desc: A tree up to 5 levels deep, autosaving about every 2 seconds. Full version history: line-level diff, preview, tagging and rollback, with history append-only. Cross-document links resolve by id, so renaming never breaks them.

items.title: Diagrams (PlantUML)
items.desc: Rendering goes through a self-hosted PlantUML server, so source never appears in a URL, a Referer header or a proxy log. 100k character cap; syntax errors come back as an annotated error image. The project's task relationship diagram is generated automatically.

items.title: Whiteboard
items.desc: An Excalidraw canvas that autosaves, storing the canvas, background and grid only. Paste accepts bitmaps only - SVG carries a script-injection risk, so it is refused. 3MB canvas cap.

items.title: Attachments
items.desc: 50MB by default, 1-500MB by platform policy. Virus scanning fails closed: if the scanner is unconfigured, unreachable or times out, the upload is rejected rather than waved through.

items.title: External links
items.desc: Off-site material is registered as a resource, so it attaches to tasks, goes to trash and gets shared like everything else.

shots.caption: Diagrams · rendered server-side, source stays out of the URL

governance.title: Permission is two layers multiplied
governance.lead: The global role (admin / user) decides which pages you can open; the project role (PM / collaborator / tester / observer) decides which tasks you can touch. The two multiply, and any role the system cannot resolve falls back to least privilege.

items.title: Admin does not mean read-everything
items.desc: Governance pages - users, logs, the project list - belong to admins; project content still goes through membership. There is no back door into a project they have not joined, and joining is itself an audited event.

items.title: The audit log records only what matters
items.desc: Five whitelisted categories: authorization, sharing, destructive actions, auth and credentials, configuration changes - plus every denied action, highlighted. Ordinary field edits go to the object's own activity feed instead. The audit log has no TTL.

items.title: One account, one session
items.desc: The newest sign-in wins. Force-logout is not an instant disconnect and does not change the password; to actually stop someone, disable the account. Accounts are never deleted - delete one and "who did this" in the audit log points at nothing.

items.title: Two fates in the trash
items.desc: Docs, diagrams, whiteboards, attachments and links are soft-deleted for 30 days. Tasks are deleted immediately and irreversibly, guarded by "a task with children cannot be deleted directly". Share links die on delete and do not come back on restore.

governance.figureCaption: Global role x project role · multiplied, not added
governance.shotCaption: Audit log · five whitelisted categories, denied actions highlighted

api.title: Other systems can <accent>subscribe</accent> to this graph
api.lead: External access happens through an external principal, not a bare API key - and it is bound by the same project membership. Scopes: specific tasks, the project root task, or assigned to me.

items.title: Six event types
items.desc: task.created / task.updated / task.status_changed / task.deleted, plus link.created / link.deleted. Both task and relationship changes are covered.

items.title: Verify raw bytes, dedupe by id
items.desc: Consumers must verify the signature against the raw request body and dedupe on the payload id - global ordering is not promised, and duplicate deliveries are allowed by design.

items.title: A backoff ladder in the open
items.desc: 1 minute, 5 minutes, 30 minutes, 2 hours, 6 hours - then the delivery is dead-lettered. The delivery log carries the failure reason.

items.title: JSON-LD semantic projection
items.desc: Two read-only endpoints: task list and task detail. Ask for JSON-LD in the Accept header and you get the semantic projection, with Vary: Accept on the response. Read only for now - there is no external write API.

items.title: One plugin per platform
items.desc: GitHub is built in. Online and offline import share the same mapping and idempotency code, so results match field by field; re-running is safe, and "created 0 / skipped 48" is a success. One-way and read-only: changes here never flow back upstream.

api.nameNote: WorkGraph is the product name; the repository, the CLI and the delivery headers all identify it as TaskGraph. Integrate against the header names above verbatim.
api.tokenNote: A token is shown in full exactly once at issue time; after that only an 8-character fingerprint remains. Issuing one is a critical audit event.
api.shotCaption: Subscriptions · external principals, scopes, token fingerprints and delivery health

platform.title: Runs on your own machines
platform.lead: The full loop runs on real projects today. One compose file brings up the whole stack, and data, diagram sources and files never leave your network.

items.title: One compose file, the whole stack
items.desc: Six services: the app, a single-instance worker, a MongoDB 7 replica set, object storage, upload virus scanning and PlantUML rendering. Only the app container is published - the other four are reachable on the stack network alone.

items.title: No aggregation on the read path
items.desc: P95 internal queries stay under 200ms: every compound index leads with projectId, ancestry is a materialised path, and progress is computed on write. Reads happen in server components, so the client has no requests to cache.

items.title: Diagram sources and file bytes stay inside
items.desc: PlantUML is self-hosted with its sandbox profile pinned. Object storage issues no presigned URLs - file bytes are proxied by the app, so it has no reason to be reachable from outside. The build makes no outbound calls either, and telemetry is off.

items.title: Upgrades are two idempotent steps
items.desc: First collections, validators and indexes, then the built-in manual - both steps are idempotent, so re-running them on upgrade writes nothing twice. Mail settings bump a version counter and take effect hot, so the worker never restarts.
